:::{#def-rule-of-inference}
#### Rule of inference

A **rule of inference** is a pattern of [logical argument](#def-logical-argument),
written with [propositions](#def-proposition) $P, Q, \ldots$ as placeholders,
whose [premises](#def-premise) [logically entail](#def-logical-entailment) its [conclusion](#def-conclusion)
whatever propositions are put in place of $P, Q, \ldots$.
It is written with its premises above a line and its conclusion below:

$$
\frac{P_1, \ldots, P_n}{Q}.
$$

:::
